name: Colombia 1990-94 (Maturana)
scopeNote: Colombia national team from the Italia 90 group stage to the USA 94 group stage, centred on the 1993-94 side (24 wins in a row per La Grinta; 5-0 in Buenos Aires, 5 Sept 1993). Style named by sources as 'toque toque' (touch-touch), zonal marking with a back four, formally 4-2-2-2 (RCN) or 4-4-2 / near-diamond (TFT, La Grinta). Tactical detail in sources is almost all from 1993-94 (5-0, Romania, USA); Italia 90 appears only in Maturana's own recollection. Start and end dates (9 June 1990 v UAE; 26 June 1994 v Switzerland) come from memory, not from a mined page; the 18 June 1994 Romania date comes from a search-result URL title. The second Maturana spell start is given only as 1993 (no day found). Many eventDates are partial (YYYY/YY or YYYY-MM) because sources give no days. Popular label 'tiki-taka of Colombia' is only a journalist's comparison (Paris Review).
openQuestions: Who coached Colombia between Italia 90 (June 1990) and Maturana return in 1992/93? Wikipedia says Maturana returned to Colombia in 1992 (América) and led the national team from 1993; the 1991 Copa America coach is unconfirmed (possibly Luis Augusto 'Chiqui' Garcia). Not listed in managers[] until verified.
Hernan Dario Gomez was assistant to Maturana in 1993-94 (RCN, El Colombiano) and was not head coach in the period; he took over after USA 94 (from memory).
Shape label disagrees: 4-2-2-2 with Valderrama behind the striker (RCN) vs 4-4-2 near diamond (La Grinta, TFT). Trivela lineup has Rincon-Gomez-Alvarez with Valderrama and two strikers, a 4-3-1-2.
Pressing: FourFourTwo and Trivela say high press, La Grinta says no all-pitch press, sequences by context; Valencia says they sat back and countered in the 2nd half of the 5-0.
Italia 90 (Higuita as sweeper-keeper, Germany 1-1) has no verified tactical page in this file; the 1990 spell is thinly covered.
Whether the 5-0 and a heavy friendlies schedule hurt preparation for USA 94 is contested (Maradona, Gomez, Maturana say the threats mattered more).
